transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-09-30 15:00 PT | Duration: 54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CloudNova - Head of Partnerships), Ken Ito (CloudNova - Platform PM), Samir Patel (CloudNova - Cloud Architect)
---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Jordan from Redwood, Priya our solutions engineer. CloudNova, who do we have?
[00:08] Marta: Hi Jordan, Marta here. Ken and Samir are with me.
[00:11] Ken: Hi.
[00:12] Samir: Hey.
[00:14] Jordan: Great. Goal for today is to align on the marketplace listing integration and the reference-arch for the joint solution, and to lock down owners and dates for the pilot. Priya will walk through recommended artifacts.
[00:26] Priya: Cool. I'll share my screen — give me a sec.
[00:31] (screen share)
[00:33] Priya: So first slide, marketplace assets. We typically need: listing metadata, logo/svg, screenshots, short and long descriptions, deployment option flags (hosted, dedicated, private), and then the packaging artifacts — Helm chart, container image location, or Terraform module.
[00:48] Marta: When you say deployment option flags, do you mean customers can choose Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private? We want to make sure our marketplace UI supports that.
[00:55] Jordan: Yep — Redwood exposes a field on the listing for supported modes. On our side we map that to SKU options for pricing. If CloudNova wants to surface both a managed integration and a self-hosted reference arch, we'll need separate SKUs.
[01:09] Ken: How does billing work for marketplace-managed deployments? Is it metered through Redwood or through CloudNova?
[01:15] Priya: Good question — for our marketplace we can support pay-per-use via Redwood's metering, or you can list an AMI/OCI image that customers self-host and billing is off-platform. For joint-managed offerings we typically do a SKU mapping so the marketplace facilitates billing to the customer and splits revenue via partner settlement -- we can share the exact flow.
[01:33] Samir: Ok that makes sense. For our customers we prefer the self-hosted option but want a managed pilot to prove integration.
[01:41] Priya: That's common — we usually recommend starting with a hosted pilot to run E2E smoke tests and perf baselines, then promote the reference-arch for self-hosting with a Helm chart or Terraform.
[01:53] Jordan: On the reference-arch side, Priya, can you walk through the network topology you recommend?
[01:58] Priya: Sure — typical pattern is VPC peering between Redwood-managed VPCs and customer VPC for private deployment, or for marketplace reference arch we provide a diagram that includes: public ingress LB (optional), private subnet worker nodes, KMS integrated for key management, SSO/SAML for identity, and an audit logging sink to the customer's logging bucket. We also include an optional sidecar for KV-cache persistence.
[02:20] Samir: KV-cache? Do you mean KV cache for the model's key value attention cache — we use a Redis cluster for that.
[02:25] Priya: Yes, exactly. Some customers use Redis; others use an in-cluster LRU cache. The diagram will call out recommended sizes and p95 latency targets.
[02:35] Marta: A couple of compliance questions — SOC2 and encryption at rest. We need to make sure the listing explicitly calls out SOC2 status and whether customer data is encrypted with customer-managed keys.
[02:45] Jordan: Redwood can attest SOC 2 Type II for the hosted product. For private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations so you can use your CMK. We'll include a security pack doc that clarifies which modes are covered.
[02:56] Ken: For the KMS integration — is that an API call to Redwood or do we mount keys in the customer environment?
[03:01] Priya: For Redwood-hosted, we integrate with customer KMS via key wrapping and BYOK flows — it's an API and service account relationship. For private/on-prem the keys stay customer-managed in their KMS and Redwood's control plane will not have access. Some of the docs can be a bit wordy — we'll send the security pack.
[03:16] Samir: Cool. On networking, we prefer VPC peering over transit gateway if possible — simpler for our infra team.
[03:23] Priya: That works. We'll model the reference arch for peering and include a TGW variant as an appendix.
[03:29] Jordan: Let's talk artifacts. Priya mentioned Helm chart and Terraform modules — what's the minimal set we need to publish on the marketplace?
[03:36] Priya: Minimal viable: a Helm chart with templated values (values.yaml), a README explaining deploy steps and required permissions, a container image in an OCI registry with tag, and a small smoke test script that validates endpoints. Optionally a Terraform module to wire up network and IAM. Also a sample policy for RBAC and an SSO integration guide.
[03:55] Marta: Do you host the image for the marketplace or do partners host their own registry?
[03:59] Jordan: Partners can either host in their registry and we reference it, or partner uploads to a partner registry we mirror. For ease we can host initial pilot images in our registry under a partner namespace.
[04:08] Ken: We need guidance on image scanning and CVE policy.
[04:11] Priya: We'll include our image-scan requirements in the security pack — must pass X severity thresholds, and we require SBOM. We'll provide an SBOM template.
[04:20] Jordan: On metadata copy — Marta, we should agree short tagline, 1-paragraph description, and three bullets of key benefits. I'll send a template.
[04:29] Marta: Perfect. We'll draft the copy.
[04:32] (slight crosstalk)
[04:34] Samir: Quick technical — when you run the hosted pilot, what metrics will you collect? We want to see latency breakdown and token costs.
[04:40] Priya: We'll collect per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, token consumption, model variant, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rates. We'll share a spreadsheet for the benchmark results. Typical pilot captures baseline with 1, 8, and 16 concurrent users to observe batching effects.
[04:56] Samir: For batching yes, we need to see worst-case p95 for single-request latencies too — some of our customers have low-latency SLOs.
[05:04] Priya: Agreed — we'll include worst-case latency tests (no batching) and a throughput test to characterize cost per token.
[05:10] Ken: Any constraints on sequence length for tests?
[05:13] Priya: We'll test with 256 and 1024 token contexts. We'll also surface quantization/FP16 differences if relevant.
[05:20] Jordan: Now on the joint solution listing — marketplace requires partner logo, support contact, and a short SLA blurb. Marta, do you have legal/resource for the partner listing agreement?
[05:30] Marta: I'll loop in our legal ops. I need the partner checklist though.
[05:34] Jordan: I'll attach the checklist in the follow-up. It includes legal contacts, support matrix, pricing model and settlement details.
[05:40] Marta: Good. Anything about single sign-on? We need to know whether customers can SSO via our IdP or if Redwood requires separate config.
[05:48] Priya: Our marketplace supports SAML and OIDC; we can provide an example IdP config. For shared SSO flows, you can either federate to Redwood or configure your IdP in the reference arch for self-hosted. We'll document both.
[06:00] Samir: There was earlier mention of a sidecar for KV cache persistence — is that supported by Redwood runtime?
[06:06] Priya: Yes, runtime supports KV caching with hooks for Redis or in-memory LRU. For private deployments we recommend Redis cluster with persistence enabled. We'll include recommended instance types and memory configs.
[06:18] Ken: Any known incompatibilities for ARM64 instances? Some of our infra uses Graviton.
[06:22] Priya: Model binary compatibility varies. We have prebuilt images for x86_64; Graviton/ARM64 is supported for some model builds but not all. We'll call that out in the listing and provide notes for compilation if you want to enable Graviton.
[06:36] Marta: From a go-to-market angle, we also want a joint solution badge and a reference architecture PDF we can co-brand.
[06:42] Jordan: Yep — we do co-branded reference arch PDFs. Priya, we'll need a high-res SVG of CloudNova's logo.
[06:48] Priya: Also, who will be the technical lead on your side for the pilot?
[06:52] Marta: Samir will lead, with Ken as PM.
[06:55] Jordan: Ok noted. Final bit — pilot plan and timeline. Proposal: Redwood spins up a hosted pilot env week of Oct 12 for 1 week of benchmarking. Prior to that we need the VPC peering details and test account by Oct 5, and we need to finalize listing copy by Oct 2. Does that work?
[07:10] Samir: Week of Oct 12 works. We'll get the network info by Oct 5.
[07:14] Marta: Legal review might slip but we'll try to have contact by Oct 6.
[07:19] Jordan: Great. Any other questions?
[07:22] Ken: One small thing — competitors. Our internal stakeholders asked how Redwood compares to ApexAI on latency and CloudOpsX on pricing. Any short bullets?
[07:31] Jordan: Short: Redwood emphasizes inference economics and deterministic latency with routing + KV caching; ApexAI focuses on model features; CloudOpsX undercuts on price but lacks dedicated runtime optimizations. We'll send a concise comparison sheet.
[07:45] Marta: Ok thanks.
[07:47] Jordan: Alright let's recap action items then we'll wrap.
[07:50] Priya: Recap: Priya will produce Helm chart and smoke test. Jordan will send marketplace checklist, pricing SKUs, and template copy. Samir will provide VPC and test creds. Marta to confirm legal contact. Schedule pilot for Oct 12.
[08:10] Jordan: I'll send calendar invites and the repo link after this call with skeleton artifacts. Thanks everyone.
[08:16] Marta: Thanks.
[08:18] Ken: Thanks all.
[08:19] Samir: Bye.
---
Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'AuroroCloud' typed once), filler words, and some speaker label ambiguity in a couple places where participants spoke over each other.
